  > 
  > Sentences in `paper/results.tex` (§5.6) and the Fig 5 caption that change, all k = 3, non-linear cells, German MLP excluded from the retraining ranges as before:
  > 
  > 1. Retraining ranges: bootstrap 0.14–0.73 (unchanged), **seed 0.40–0.88** (was 0.50–0.88; the new low is ACS-Employment MLP, 0.404), hyperparameter 0.14–0.70 (unchanged). ACS-Employment MLP: bootstrap 0.29, seed 0.40, hyperparameter 0.34.
  > 2. Explainer floor at the reference budget 0.91–0.99, at the small budget 0.62–0.90, background floor 0.27–0.69: unchanged (ACS-Employment MLP: 0.96, 0.72, 0.58). "In every non-linear cell the explainer floor at the reference budget is above the background floor and above all three retraining floors" still holds.
  > 3. "K = 10 retrained models, fewer where the AUC filter kept fewer": add ACS-Employment MLP, K = 6 in all three definitions (open markers). The Fig 5 caption "the ACS Employment MLP is absent" is no longer true: it is present, with n = 30 instances.
  > 4. Paired Kernel vs two backgrounds at the reference budget: 14 non-linear cells now (German MLP excluded, as for the 13), the paired difference excludes zero in **7 of 14** (5 where floor b is higher, 2 lower: GMSC RF and MLP). ACS-Employment MLP is unresolved (+0.03, CI −0.06 to 0.13). Including German MLP (unresolved too) it is 7 of 15.
  > 5. Median over cells with all four backgrounds: **19 cells**, B20 0.46, B50 0.61, **B200 0.74** (was 0.75), **k-means50 0.82** (was 0.77). The German MLP will make it 20; I will restate then.
  > 6. Appendix, floor (b) by background: "below the run-to-run agreement of the `shap` default in every d ≥ 16 row" holds for random-row backgrounds (B20, B50, B200) in all 28 default-budget and 76 largest-sampled rows, but not for k-means50: ACS-Employment MLP with k-means50 has floor b 0.87 against floor a 0.93, difference −0.05 with CI −0.19 to 0.04 (default budget), and −0.11 with CI −0.25 to 0.00 (largest sampled budget). Against the paired Kernel estimator: positive in 16 of 28 default rows (CI above 0 in 9, below 0 in 7) and 40 of 76 largest-sampled rows (CI above 0 in 33, below 0 in 33).
  > 
  > CPU-hours: the platform ledger shows 1.15 CPU-h for these four jobs. The 34 CPU-h I gave earlier included the jobs then running, so "about 34" stands, to within about 1–2 CPU-h, until the German MLP job ends; I will say so then. Keep the paper's "about 24 / about 34".
